Friday, the 27th April, 2007/ 7 Vaisakha, 1929 (Saka)                                                                        
The House met at eleven of the clock, 
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair. 
OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, we have learnt with sorrow the passing away 
of Mr. Boris Nikolaevich Yeltsin, former President of the Russian Federation. 
A courageous man, he will be remembered as the First President of the Russian 
Federation, who steered the country through difficult times of transition, and as 
the one who laid the foundation of a renewed partnership between India and the 
Russian Federation. 
This House joins the leadership and the people of the Russian Federation in 
mourning the passing away of former President Yelts in and conveys deep 
condolences to his family. 
I request members to rise in their places and obser ve silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members of the 
bereaved family our deep sense of sorrow and sympathy.

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
Debt-burden and suicide in Punjab 
 362. DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANfA: ††  
SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH: 
.    Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether a suicide census,, conducted by NGO namely 'Movement 
Against State Repression' found that 1360 farmers had committed suicide in just 
one district of Punjab in a span of 17 years due to debt-burden; 
(b) if so, what is the average debt-burden on a farmer-household in the State 
and how it compares with other States and country as a whole; 
(c) the total number of such suicides in the State duri ng the last five years; 
and 
(d) the steps taken to stop such suicides? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a ) to 
(d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a)-The NGO, named Movement Against State Repressio n (MASR) has 
claimed that it had conducted a census in Munak sub -division of Sangrur 
District, covering all the 93 villages with a time frame of 19 years (1988 to 
2006). It claims that 1276 persons committed suicide in rural areas of the sub-
division, during the period. However, causes of sui cides have not been 
analysed in the report. In this regard, the Governm ent of Punjab was 
requested on 20.4.2007 to send their report on the matter which is awaited. 
(b) As per NSSO Report No. 498, §9th Round (January-December, 2003), the 
amount of outstanding loan per farmer household for all classes for Punjab was 
Rs. 41,576.00, against the all India average of Rs. 12,585.00. Similarly the number 
of farmer households having outstanding loan were 12.07 lakh against the all 
India number of 434.24 lakh. In terms of percentage , 65.4% farmer 
households were indebted in Punjab against the all India average of 48.6%. 
††The question was actually asked on the floor of the. House by Dr. Gyan 
Prakash Pilania- 
2 

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) As per information furnished by the State Governmen t during the last 
five years (2001-2005), 55 farmers committed suicide. 
(d) Agriculture being a state subject, it is primarily the responsibility of the 
State Government concerned to provide various servi ces to farmers. The 
Government of India supports and supplements the St ate's efforts through 
various policy measures and schemes/programmes. These, inter-alia, include the 
announcement of a credit policy in the  year 2004 to double the flow of credit to 
the agriculture sector in three years. From Kharif 2006-07, farmers are being 
provided crops loans up to Rs. 3 lakh at 7% rate of  interest. The Government 
has also announced a package for revival of cooperative credit structure. A major 
effort has been initiated for diversification of ag riculture. National Horticulture 
Mission has been launched since the year 2005 for ensuring end-to-end approach 
with backward and forward linkages covering research, post harvest management, 
processing and marketing, which is expected to impr ove the income level of 
farmers. Besides Government announces each season Minimum Support Prices 
(MSPs) for major agricultural commodities and organ izes purchase 
operations through public and cooperative agencies so that the market prices do 
not fail below MSPs and farmers interests are protected. 
DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: Mr. Chairman, Sir, I woul d like to 
make a submission to the hon. Agriculture Minister,  who is known to be the 
messiah of farmers. Is it not an irony, your honour , that when India joins the 
Trillion-Dollar Club, Indian farmer; Annandata, is forced to commit harakiri. Is 
the suicide by farmers' scenario.not horrendous, alarming and tragic? Is it not 
surprising that in Punjab; the granary of India, ha rdy Jaffa is resorting to 
atmahatya? In the reply, the hon. Minister has mentioned that 1276 persons have 
committed suicide in rural areas of one sub-division of Punjab only during the last 19 
years. However, causes of suicides have not been analysed. Who will analyse 
them? Do causes need analysis? Does a farmer commit  suicide because of 
pleasure and insanity? It is obvious.... 
MR. CHAIRMAN; Let him reply. 
DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: This is the first question, Sir. 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: Sir, the hon. Member has said th at 1276 
persons have committed suicide. This is neither the statement of the 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
Government nor the State Government. This is the statement of an NGO, named 
Movement Against State Repression. They have submitted this statement. The 
State Government sent a communication to me. There were two 
communications. One specific communication is about the cotton farmers in 
Malwa in the State. In five years, 55 farmers have committed suicide in Punjab, 
that is one statement. And, about this question par ticularly, the Punjab 
Government has communicated: "Give us time, we are going to give detailed 
information to Parliament. We are not in a position to submit all this detailed 
report." So, it is mentioned that the report is awaited. 
DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: Sir, my second supplementary is this. Is it 
not enough if 55 farmers commit suicide? As far as ail India figures are concerned, 
Sir, I would like to remind you that out of 1,87,000 suicides in a year, 15.8 per 
cent were farmers' suicides. 
And, that comes to more than 16,000 every year—it i s, daily, 45, and it is 
monthly, 1430. Is it not enough to make us shudder? Is it not enough to make us 
rise and do something. For the last few years we ha ve been hearing that they 
are doing something but nothing is happening. As far as. 31 districts of Andhra 
Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Punjab and Kerala are concerned, there is a 
constant spate of hundreds and hundreds. I have figures with me given by the 
Government, and if we read them, you will find it to be a very odd scenario. What 
will happen, how will it happen? Mr. Chairman, Sir,  you have also been 
expressing great concern about it. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Everybody including the Minister has been expressing great 
concern. 
DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: Then, Sir, something shou ld happen. I 
know the hon. Minister has thinned down because of this. But something must 
happen. 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR; Sir, this question is about one particular State. 
There is no reference to the whole nation. But I ac cept one thing that Punjab 
Government has gone in details. They have appointed  Punjab State Farmers' 
Commission under the Chairmanship of Dr. G.S. Kalkar. The Chairman of the 
Commission has submitted the report to the State Go vernment but the State 
Government has not taken any action yet.. 
4 

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
But the hon. Chief Minister, Shri Prakash Singh Badal, has communicated that the 
Punjab Government is taking this issue very seriously. They have constituted one 
team of some senior officers. They would like to submit a detailed proposal to 
the Prime Minister, the Agriculture Minister and th e Finance Minister of this 
country. The Government of India has appointed one Committee under the 
Chairmanship of Shri Radhakrishnan where this issue will be discussed in depth 
and some recommendations would be given to the Gove rnment of India. The 
Punjab Government would like to submit their entire report and their demands 
to the Radhakrishnan Commission. They are saying th at within another 10—
15 days they will complete all these details, and, then I will be able to answer 
what exactly the action the Government of India is going to take.

DR. RC. ALEXANDER: Sir, my question to the hon. Minister is, instead of 
waiting for the reports on the incidence of suicides in these places, can we not ask 
the State Government to use the Revenue Officers to make a quick survey of the 
area for which they are responsible, assess the nature of hardship from which these 
people suffer, particularly, because of indebtedness and collect those details and 
immediately ask, at least, the Government banks to write off the interest burden 
accruing on this? We welcome all the Committees that the Minister referred to, but 
Mr. Minister, I feel that if this responsibility is squarely placed on the Collectors, 
Sub-Collectors and the Tehsildars, within one month, you will be able to get a list of 
people who are suffering from acute indebtedness and who are prone to suicide 
dangers, and assure these people, firsthand, by these Revenue Officials that their 
interest burden will be written off. And, if this approach is followed, I feel the 
number of of suicides can be brought down to very minimum levels. 
6 

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: Sir, as I mentioned regarding the efforts made by 
the Punjab Government in this connection, the Punja b Government appointed 
the Punjab State Farmers Commission. Through the Farmers Commission, the 
Punjab Government has assigned this particular job to one of the Chandigarh-
based organisations. Their report has come. In that report, certain things have been 
communicated. The distinctive features of suicide cases, which emerge because of 
the study, are: first, indebtedness was reported as a major cause of suicide by 
thirty per cent of the victim families, followed by  conflicts at home and poor 
financial position of the household; second, eighty -six per cent of the victims 
were actually under debt; third, a majority of suic ide victims were small and 
marginal farmers; fourth, a majority of suicide victims were illiterate and semi-
literate; fifth, a vast majority of victims belonged to young and middle-age groups; 
sixth, a majority of suicide victims had borrowed money from informal credit 
agencies; and seventh, declining income due to ever -increasing cost of 
production and stagnant farm productivity and output prices and high amount of debt 
were reported to be the major causes of the non-payment of the loan. 
So, Sir, these are the issues which are ultimately identified and on the basis of 
that, the Punjab Government would make a recommendation as to what action it 
is going to take on this issue and what expectation It has from the Government of 
India. The hon. Member has suggested that the State Government should take 
action within thirty days. Sir, the State Governmen t has communicted to me 
that within fifteen days, it will send all these de tails on the action from their 
side and the demand which it wants to make to the Government of India. 
SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Sir, the Government of India 
has announced a package in the name of Prime Minist er's package to the 
affected areas, covering 31 districts in three Stat es. According to me, it 
has not yielded any results. I would like to know f rom the hon. Minister 
whether any impact assessment has been done on the Prime Minister's 
package. In spite of this package, in my own State,  around 5000 people 
have committed suicide in the past three years, Wha t action has been 
taken on it?   
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: I would like to request for a separate question here 
because that is a different question. This question relates particularly to Punjab. 
7 

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Sir, Prime Ministe r's 
package with regard to farmers' suicide is a releva nt question. Is Punjab not a 
part of India?

Statement  
A Committee was constituted by the Delhi High Court  for review of the 
Transplantation of Human Organs Act (THOA), 1994, a nd Rules framed 
thereunder. The recommendations of the Committee have been put on the website 
of the Ministry. After examining the recommendation s of the Committee, it 
was felt that wider consultation with stakeholders will be advisable and a 
national consultation on the subject will be held in May, 2007.

pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that per capita availability of cultivable land in the 
country has declined from 0.27 hectares in 1980 to 0.16 hectares in 2005; 
(b) if so, how the Central Government are persuading th e States to 
formulate suitable legislation to bring more and more land under cultivation and 
use less agriculture land for non-agricultural purposes such as roads, industries, 
etc; and 
(c) to what extent Government's Watershed Development Programmes such as 
National Watershed Development Project for Rainfed Areas, Soil Conservation 
for Enhancing Productivity in Degraded lands, Integ rated Wasteland 
Development Programme, etc. have helped it in bringing more and more area 
under cultivation? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to 
(c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House 
Statement  
(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. As per available estimates, th e per capita availability of 
cultivable land has declined from 0.27 ha. in 1980- 81 to 0.17 ha in 2004-05 
due to increase in population and diversion of agricultural land for non agricultural 
purposes such as urbanization, roads, industries etc. There is a marginal decline in 
agricultural land from 185.09 million ha. in 1980-81 
17 

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
to 183.09 million ha. in 2004-05. During the same p eriod, land under non-
agricultural purposes has increased from 19.66 million ha. to 24.45 million ha. 
As per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, Land and Water 
falls under the purview of State Government, therefore, it is for the States to bring 
about suitable legislation regarding regulation of conversion of agricultural land for 
non-agricultural purposes. However, Government of India is implementing a 
Centrally Sponsored Programme of State Land Use Boa rds (SLUBs) through 
Macro Management of Agriculture (MMA). Under this P rogramme, State 
Governments have been advised to bring suitable leg islation to prevent use of 
agricultural land for non-agricultural purposes. Some of the States, through their 
SLUBs have issued instructions and executive orders relating to diversion of 
agricultural land for non-agricultural purposes. 
Government of India is also implementing various Wa tershed 
Development Programmes, namely, (i) National Watershed Development Project 
for Rainfed Areas (NWDPRA), (ii) Soil Conservation for Enhancing the 
Productivity of Degraded Lands in the Catchments of River Valley Project and 
Flood Prone River (RVP & FPR), (iii) Reclamation of  Alkali Soils (RAS), (iv) 
Watershed Development Projects for Shifting Cultivations Areas (WDPSCA), (v) 
Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP), (vi) Desert Development Programme 
(DDP), (vii) Integrated Wasteland Development Proje ct (IWDP), (viii) 
Watershed Development Fund (WDF) and (ix) Externall y Aided Projects 
(EAPs) for development of degraded lands in the cou ntry. Under these 
programmes, since inception upto Tenth Five Year Plan, an area of about 50.83 
million ha. of degraded lands have been developed as per scheme-wise details 
given in Statement-I (See below). 
Parts of such developed lands are also brought under cultivation to maintain 
balance in different types of land uses as evident from Land Use Statistics given in 
Statement-ll (See below). Inspite of an increase of about 5.00 million ha. in non-
agricultural uses, the net sown area has increased by about 1.06 million ha. from 
1980-91 to 2004-05. Similarly, the barren lands hav e been reduced by about 
2.22 million ha. in the same period. Culturable was te land has also decreased 
by about 2.5 million ha. in the same period. The fo rest area has increased by 
about 2.00 million ha. during this period.

Subsidy on Export of Sugar  
†*365. SHRI PYARELAL KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of 
CONSUMERAFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided t o give subsidy on 
export of sugar; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the likely financial burden on Government due to the same? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMERAFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to (c) AStatement is laid on the 
Table of the House. 
Statement  
(a) to (c) The Government have decided to provide export assistanice to defray 
the cost of internal transport and freight charges,  marketing and handling 
charges at a flat rate of Rs. 1350 per tonne on exp ort of domestically 
manufactured sugar from sugar factories located in the coastal States and at the flat 
rate of Rs. 1450 per tonne from sugar factories loc ated in Other than the coastal 
States. Exports made under Open General License (OGL) only (and not under 
'advance license') on or after 19th April, 2007 and upto 18th April, 2008 or till 
further orders, whichever is earlier,

Crop loss due to rains, hailstorm, etc. 
†*368. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the Minister of AGRIC ULTURE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the crops of wheat, musta rd and green 
vegetables in some parts of the country have suffered due to unseasonal rains, 
hailstorm, storms and snowfall in March, 2007; 
(b) if so, what steps have been taken by Government to compensate the loss 
caused to the farmers; and 
(c) the amount, so far, provided to the farmers by Government to take them 
out of these disasters? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to 
(c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 Statement  
(a) to (c) The Governments of Haryana, Madhya Prade sh, Punjab, 
Rajasthan and Uttarakhand reported damage / loss to crops due to untimely rains and 
hailstorms. The State-wise position is as under: 
(i) Haryana 
The Government of Haryana have reported damage of 25% or more to wheat, 
paddy, cotton, mustard and other crops in an area of about 5.78

lakh acres due to heavy rains and hailstorms during February and March, 2007. 
(ii) Madhya Pradesh 
The Government of Madhya Pradesh have reported crop loss of 5% to 50% in 
1,74 lakh hectares due to untimely rains and hailst orm in 35 districts in the 
State. 
(iii) Punjab 
The Government of Punjab have reported that crops in an area of 2.15 lakh 
acres were damaged due to untimely rains and hailst orms during 
February/March, 2007. As per available information,  the untimely rains and 
hailstorms caused damage to wheat, potato, cauliflower and sunflower. 
(iv) Rajasthan 
As per available information, the hailstorms in Feb ruary and March, 2007, 
caused damage to wheat, mustard, barley , bengal gr am, cumin, isabgol and 
summer.vegetable crops in about 2.85 lakh hectares. 
(v) Uttarakhand 
The Government of Uttarakhand have reported that hailstorm during March, 
2007, caused damage to rabi crops in 1:54 hectares. 
2. It is primarily the responsibility of the State Government concerned to take 
necessary measures in the wake of natural calamitie s including hailstorms. 
There is ready availability of funds with the State s under Calamity Relief Fund 
(CRF) to take necessary measured The Government of India and State 
Governments concerned contribute to CRF in the rati o of 3:1. Additional 
assistance, over and above CRF is considered from t he National Calamity 
Contingency Fund (NCCF), if necessary, for natural calamities of severe nature, 
in accordance with an established procedure, on submission of a Memorandum 
for assistance from the NCCF by the State Government. 
3. The Government of Haryana had submitted a Memorandu m seeking 
assistance from the NCCF, in the wake of hailstorm. However, it was

any Memorandum for assistance from the NCCF in the wake of hailstorms.

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
Plundering of coal from goods train  
†*369.   SHRI MOTI LALVORA:†† 
SHRI SATYAVRAT CHATURVEDI: 
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that a hug e quantity of coal 
was plundered from a goods train at the outer of No rthern Railway and North 
Central Railway near Palwal railway station on 16th-17th March, 2007; 
(b) the time span within which the plundering was commi tted by the 
plunderers; 
(c) whether this incident was reported to the Railway Protection Force; 
(d) if so, the action taken by the Railway Protection F orce and the number 
of persons arrested; and 
(e) since when this plundering of coal has been taking place and when this 
case came in cognizance of Government? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI R. 
VELU): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha. 
Statement  
(a) No, Sir. No such incident of plundering of coal in huge quantity from a 
goods train near Palwal railway station was reported on 16th-17th March, 2007. 
(b) Does not arise. 
(c) No, Sir. 
(d) to (e) Do not arise.

be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the traders in the country are feeding on high food 
prices but the farmers are made to starve due to Go vernment policy of not 
making any increase in the MPS of pulses, oil-seeds and rice; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that although the price of tur dal has increased by Rs.

the farmers; and

THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SHARAD PAWAR): (a ) to 
(c) The Government fixes the Minimum Support Prices  (MSPs) for various 
agricultural commodities, including pulses, oilseed s and paddy, taking into 
account the recommendations of Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices 
(CACP), the views of State Governments and concerne d Central Ministries as 
well as other relevant factors, which in the opinion of 
35 

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
the Government, are Important for fixation of MSPs. The MSP thus fixed is a 
guaranteed minimum price which the farmers are offered by the designated Central 
and State agencies in the event market prices tend to fall below that level. 
However, if the market price is more than the MSP f ixed by the Government, 
farmers are free to realize a higher price by selli ng their produce in the open 
market. 
With the amendment of the Agricultural Produce Mark eting Committee 
(APMC) Act for deregulation of the marketing system , the farmers now have 
more options to sell their produce to the prospective buyers. As a result of this 
and the emerging demand-supply gap, the prices in t he market during the 
harvesting season also are ruling above MSP and benefiting the farmers.

*370. SHRI BHAGIRATHI MAJHI: Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT 
AND FORESTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have done base line survey of the Greenhouse Gas 
Emissions from different sources in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
44 

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) if not, what is the source of data and its authenticity on the emissions; and 
. (d) whether Government have any plan to institute study on India's carbon dioxide 
and other green house gases emission levels? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) 
to (d) Abase line survey of Greenhouse Gas Emission of anthropogenic origin at 
1994 level was conducted for India's Initial National Communication to the United 
Nations Frame-work Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) as required under 
Article 12.1 of the UNFCCC. The Greenhouse Gas Emissions by sources and 
removals by sinks were estimated using internationally accepted methodology 
for different sectors like Energy, Industrial Proce sses, Agriculture, Land-use, 
Land-use change and Forestry and Waste. In 1994, the aggregate net Greenhouse 
Gas Emissions from the anthropogenic activities in India from the above 
mentioned sectors amounted to about 793 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide, 18 
million tonnes of methane and 0.17 million tonnes of nitrous oxide. The total carbon-
dioxide equivalent emissions amount to 4% of the global total. On per capita basis 
carbon-dioxide emissions from India was 23% of global average and only 4% of 
the United States of America, 8% of Germany, 9% of the United Kingdom and 
10% of Japan. Sector-wise Greenhouse Emissions are provided in the Statement (See 
below). Plans to study India's carbondioxide and other Greenhouse Gas Emission 
at 2000 level have been completed.

Price control of medicines  
†*371.   SHRISHREEGOPALVYAS: 
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL APTE: 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be p leased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had brought me dicines under price 
control in order to make available medicines to common man at low prices; 
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that in spite of a nnouncement by 
Government the prices of medicines were not reduced  by pharmaceutical 
companies; 
(c) if so, the details of such companies thereof; 
(d) whether any action has been taken by Government aga inst such 
companies; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof and the outcome thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI RAM VILAS 
PASWAN): (a) Yes, Sir. The Drug Policy as announced  from time-to-time is 
directed towards making available quality drugs at reasonable prices to the poor. 
The 74 bulk drugs specified in the First Schedule o f the Drugs (Prices Control) 
Order, 1995 (DPCO, 95) and the formulations based thereon are under price control 
and their prices are fixed/revised by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing 
Authority (NPPA) in accordance with the provisions of the DPCO, 95. These drugs 
have been kept under price control on the basis of criteria mentioned in 
'Modifications in Drug Policy, 1986', announced in September, 1994. The price 
fixation/revision of the Scheduled Drugs and formul ations is a continuous 
process under DPCO, 95. In case of any violation of the price fixed by NPPA, 
action for recovery of overcharging amount is taken by NPPA. Hence, prices of 
medicines under price control have been effectively controlled and kept low. 
Prices of non-Scheduled formulations are fixed by t he manufacturers 
themselves keeping in view the various factors like  cost of production, 
marketing/selling expenses, R&D expenses, trade commission, market 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
48 

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
competition, product innovation, product quality etc. Prices of these drugs are 
regularly monitored and corrective measures taken where public interest is found to 
be adversely affected. 
(b) to (e) Pharma Industry Associations had voluntarily agreed to reduce trade 
margins in the case of generic drugs being sold by them. As such prices of 886 
packs of such medicines were reduced by 11 pharma c ompanies. A 
compilation of a list of 886 such medicines, whose prices were voluntarily 
agreed to be reduced by eleven companies, is availa ble en this Department's 
Website www.chemicals.gov.in. It  has also been placed in the library of the 
Parliament. The list covers formulations in all dos age forms such as tablets, 
capsules and syrups, etc. and they find usage in th e treatment of a large 
number of diseases. The medicines covered are antib iotics, cough syrups, 
painkillers as well as those used during the surgical operations, for the cure of 
the infectious diseases and for the treatment of hypertension etc. 
The revised prices of these 886 packs were to be im plemented by the 
companies on packs manufactured after 2nd October/2nd November, 2006. A 
survey of the prices of these medicines in selected cities was got done through 
the pharma PSUs on 22.2.2007 and feedback was also received from some of the 
companies. As per the findings of this survey out of 886 medicines, 258 medicines 
(of 9 companies) with reduced prices are available in the Delhi market. In other cities 
also some of these products are available at reduced prices. Most of the companies 
have informed that availability of the medicines with reduced prices would depend 
on depletion of their old stocks with the Distributors. 
The survey conducted by Hindustan Antibiotics Ltd. revealed that out of 11 
companies price have been reduced by 9 companies in case of some of the packs. 
In case of two companies i.e. Cipla Ltd., and Lupin Ltd. only the old stock was 
available without any price reduction. 
This reduction has been done on a voluntary basis b y the companies. It is 
proposed to streamline the system of trade margins through the proposed National 
Pharmeceuticals Policy. 
It was noticed that out of 886 medicine packs there was a violation of DPCO, 
95 in case of prices of 97 packs. NPPA has directed the respective companies to 
explain the reasons for violations of the respective provisions

*374. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJARY: Will the Minister of  
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact a study conducted by the C entre for Science 
and Environment has indicated that many of the rive rs in the country are 
headed towards an environmental disaster; 
(b) if so, the details of the report and Government's response thereto; 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
51 

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
(c) whether it is a fact that a large number of sewage treatment plants in the 
country do not meet the standards for the discharge of effluents; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof alongwith the details of  the projects set up to 
clean major rivers, funds earmarked, spent and results achieved, so far, project-
wise? 
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI A. RAJA): (a) 
and (b) The study entitled "Sewage Canal - How to Clean the Yamuna" by the 
Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) deals with the problem of sewage 
generation and disposal and the increasing pollution levels in the river Yamuna, 
among some of the other rivers. The report suggests  ensuring measures such as 
prudent water use through a package of fiscal measu res, decentralization of 
sewage treatment, reuse and recycling of treated sewage, improved utilization of 
STPs and achievement of a minimum flow, including survey of water bodies & 
programme for rejuvenation of water bodies to impro ve water storage & water 
flow in the rivers. The ever increasing pollution load due to excessive growth of 
population calls for concerted effort by all the ag encies concerned by way of 
budgetary and non-budgetary commitments, inter-sectoral coordination, revenue 
generation for maintenance of assets by introduction of user charges, & adoption 
of site-specific strategies. The CSE is a NGO and while its recommendations would 
be studied with intent, they cannot bind the policy  and fiscal actions of the 
Government. 
(c) As per a report of Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB 2006), there 
are 231 Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) at present w orking in Class-I, Class-
ll cities & other smaller towns in the country. Besides, 38 are under construction. 
The notified effluent standards for STPs for discharge in surface water bodies are: 
Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD)-30 miligrams per li tre and Total 
Suspended Solids (TSS)-100 miligrams per litre.and Chemical Oxygen 
Demand (COD)-250mg/L. Based on the performance eval uation of 115 STPs 
carried out by CPCB, 70 STPs were reported to achie ve the standards for 
discharge in surface water. 
(d) The National River Conservation Plan (NRCP) is under implementation for 
undertaking pollution abatement works in the major rivers of the country and at 
present covers 34 rivers with works undertaken in 160 towns spread in 20 States at 
an approved cost of Rs. 4783 crore. Under this Plan, the

Industries polluting river Bagad  
†*375. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will the Minister of ENVI RONMENT 
AND FORESTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the action taken by Government during last ten months against 
Jubilant Organosys Ltd., Ramganga Fertilizers, etc. which pollute the Bagad river 
a tributary of river Ganga at Jyotibaphule Nagar; 
(b) if no action has been taken, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) by when Government would take action to close these  factories 
(industries) alongwith the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI A. RAJA): 
(a) and (b) As per the information available on record, the UP State Pollution Control 
Board has been regularly monitoring industrial poll ution in respect of M/s. 
Jubilant Organosys Ltd. and M/s. Ram Ganga Fertilizers located at Jyotiba Phule 
Nagar in Uttar Pradesh. During June 23, 2006 to April 11, 2007, the SPCB has 
inspected the industries ten times. 
The distillery unit of M/s. Jubilant Organosys Ltd.  has installed Effluent 
Treatment Plant containing units namely, Anaerobic Microbial Digester, 
Biological Control Reactor, Methane Up Flow Reactor, Secondary Treatment System, 
Reverse Osmosis Plant, Storage Arrangement, etc. The treated effluent is being 
utilized for bio-composting as well as ferti-irrigation. Effluent generated from its 
chemical unit is treated in Combined Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) and the 
treated effluent is recycled within plant after tre atment. The effluent from the 
fertilizer unit (formerly known as Ramganga Fertili zer) is also treated and 
recycled in the process. 
Directions were issued on October 10, 2006 for further improvement of the 
pollution control arrangement namely, installation of multi effect evaporator, 
additional Reverse Osmosis Plant and increase in Bi o-composting capacity by 
the distillery unit. As per the available informati on the. industries unit has 
complied with the directions by installation of new  tube-well for dilution of 
effluent for ferti-irrigation, and is also in the process of complying with installation 
of additional Riverse Osmosis Plant in addition to the existing one. Periodic 
inspections were also conducted by the local admini stration during December, 
2006 and January, 2007 and no discharge of effluent  from these industries in 
Bagad river was reported.

Statement  
Precautionary steps taken in the country as part of preparedness- and to 
prevent outbreaks of bird flu in India  
Measures taken in the country as part of preparedness and to prevent bird flu 
outbreak in India are as follows:— 
1. A clear and focused National Strategy for preparedn ess, control and 
containment has been formulated. The immediate prio rity is to 
minimize the public health risk by containing Al at  source i.e. the 
animal by halting further spread of epidemic in pou ltry population. 
Based on the outbreak experience, a detailed Action  Plan (first 
developed by the Department in 2005) has been revised and circulated to the 
States in November, 2006 to undertake control and containment operations. 
2. Surveillance is continuing throughout the country. More than 1,25,000 
samples have been tested after 18th February, 2006 (first outbreak of 
Avian Influenza in India). 
3. A mechanism to provide immediate reporting of unusu al mortality is 
continued to be operationalized by which such information is collected by 
GOI Liaison Officers from States. Weekly reports on  disease situation 
are being hosted on the Departmental website. 
4. Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) have been constituted a t level of 
Government of India (Central RRTs) and State Governments (State RRTs) 
to combat outbreaks, if any. 
5. The preparedness oHhe States is being continually a ssessed and 
monitored by the GOI through video-conferences, Nat ional 
Conferences of Animal Husbandry Secretaries, regula r touring by GOI 
officers, weekly reports on unusually mortality from States etc. 
6. Ready Reckoners have been developed by GOI for situ ation analysis of 
preparedness by States. 
7. Joint mechanisms between key stakeholder Department s of GOI 
especially Animal Husbandry and Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare (MOHFW) have been operationalised at various levels and are 
working successfully. The Committee of Secretaries (COS) 
67 

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
headed by the Cabinet Secretary periodically reviews the situation. The 
Inter-Ministerial Task Force is reviewing the situation regularly. The Joint 
Monitoring Group is meeting frequently to review and decide on technical 
matters. 
8. Reserves of essential material for control operatio ns have been 
developed and are being expanded further. 
9. The Department is maintaining a strategic reserve o f Avian Influenza 
vaccines for poultry, though vaccination has not yet been applied in the 
country. 
 
10. The Department has trained more than 22,000 veterin ary manpower to 
handle control and containment operations. States h ave been advised to 
utilize the master trainers so available to train other veterinary staff. 
11. Testing of serum samples has been started at region al level in the 
laboratories at Bangalore, Kolkata, Pune and Jallandhar. 
12. The Government has announced and demonstrated its p olicy to 
compensate poultry farmers for the poultry killed in operations. 
13. High Security Animal Disease Laboratory (HSADL), Bhopal is stocked with 
required reagents. 
14. A Project of Rs. 134.78 corores for preparedness, c ontrol and 
containment of Al has been approved which will obta in World Bank 
funding. 
15. Information, Education, Communication (IEC) campaig ns have been 
carried out jointly by MOHFW and this Department in print and 
electronic media. 
An exercise has been initiated in collaboration wit h UNICEF and 
Wetlands International to develop vulnerability mapping depicting areas 
under threat of Al for use as a planning tool. 
A system has been put in place since 2004 to ban im ports from 
countries reporting Al. 
In view of the outbreak inthe neighboring countries , the following 
measures have been taken:— 
a. Ban on import of all livestock products related to poultry and

swine from the affected countries. 
b. Border States of Pakistan, Myanmar and Banglades h have been 
alerted. 
c. States have been advised to increase surveillanc e, especially 
around water bodies, advise farmers to keep poultry  indoors; 
prevent intermingling of poultry with other species ; report unusual 
mortality immediately; intensify vigilance across b order to prevent 
trade especially illegal in restricted items. 
d. Border security forces and customs filed formati ons have been 
alerted. 
e. Information, Education, Communication (IEC) camp aign has been 
stepped up in bordering States.

Statement  
Salient features of the major schemes under implementation in the  
State of Goa:  
I. Macro Management of Agriculture Scheme. 
* Provide flexibility to the States to develop and pursue the activities 
on the basis of their regional priorities, and fina lize their sector-wise 
allocation as per requirements of their development priorities, 
• Achieve decentralization in pursuance of restoring primacy of States in 
agricultural development planning; and 
• Encourage the States to adopt new initiatives for a griculture 
development under the Scheme subject to the prescribed criteria. 
II. Integrated Scheme on Oilseeds, Pulses, Oil Palm  and Maize 
(ISOPOM) 
• Increase the production and productivity of oilse eds, pulses, oilpalm 
and maize in the country so as to achieve self-suffciency in these crops.

regionally differentiated approach.

* Provide holistic grant of horticulture sector by ad option of area based 
regionally differentiated strategies which include technology 
promotion, extension, post harvest management, proc essing and 
marketing, in consonance with comparative advantage of each State/ region 
and its diverse agro-climatic feature; 
* Enhance horticulture production improve nutritional  security and 
income support to farm households; 
* Establish convergence and synergy among multiple on -going and 
planned programs for horticulture development; 
* Promote, develop and disseminate technologies, through a seamless blend of 
traditional wisdom and modern scientific knowledge; and 
* Create opportunities for employment generation for skilled and 
unskilled persons, especially unemployed youth. 
IV.Micro Irrigation 
* Provide Micro irrigation technology for enhancing water use efficiency; 
* Enhance productivity of crop, improve nutritional security and enhance the 
income level of small and marginal farmers with the driving motto of "More 
crop per drop of water"; 
* Provide appropriate mechniasm and facilities for ex tending the 
technical support to micro irrigation; and 
* Adopt system for application of fertilizer and pesticides. 
V. Support to State Extension Programmes for Extension Reforms 
* Provide decentralized and demand driven extension s ervices to farmers 
through active involvement of farmers and other stakeholders; 
* Provide national level training support for senior and middle level 
functionaries engaged in extension activities; and 
* Ensure that the policies in agriculture reflect nat ional commitment to 
empowerment of women through strategy of main streaming and strategy 
of agenda setting.

†2757. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be 
pleased to state:

decrease; 
(b) the extent of decrease in the cultivable land in various States;

(d) whether shrinkage of cultivable land is the main re ason for fall in the 
production of foodgrains; and 
(e) the steps being taken by Government for boostin g agricultural 
production? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTUR E 
(SHRI KANTI LAL BHURIA): (a) to (e) Yes, Sir. As pe r available 
estimates, there is a marginal decline in cultivabl e land from 185.09 million 
ha. in 1980-81 to 183.09 million ha. in 2004-05 due  to increase in population 
and diversion of agricultural land for non agricult ural purposes such as 
urbanization, roads, industries etc. The cultivable  land in eleven States 
namely, Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
100 

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, Punjab, R ajasthan, Tamil Nadu 
and West Bengal has marginally decreased in 2004-05  as compared to 2000-
01. 
As per Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, Land and Water falls 
under the purview of State Government, therefore, it is for the States to bring 
about suitable legislation regarding regulation of conversion of agricultural 
land for non-agricultural purposes. Government of I ndia is implementing a 
Centrally Sponsored Programme of State Land Use Boa rds (SLUBs) through 
which State Governments have been advised to bring suitable legislation to 
prevent use of agricultural and for non-agricultura l purposes. Some of the 
States, through their SLUBs have issued instruction s and executive orders to 
the line departments of their Government to ensure that prime agricultural land is 
not diverted for non-agricultural purposes. 
Though there has been a marginal decline in the cul tivable land in 2004-
05 as compared to 1980-81, the net sown area has mo re or less remained the 
same or slightly increased by 1.06 million ha. duri ng this period which 
mainly contribute to the foodgrain production. Duri ng recent years, the 
vagaries of weather have been mainly responsible fo r affecting the foodgrain 
production in the country. The Government of India is implementing various 
Schemes/Programmes namely, National Watershed Devel opment Project for 
Rainfed Areas (NWDPRA), Soil Conservation for Enhan cing Producivity of 
Degraded Lands in the Catchments of River Valley Pr oject and Flood Prone 
River (RVP & FPR), Watershed Development Project fo r Shifting 
Cultivation Area (WDPSCA), Reclamation of Alkali So ils (RAS), Drought 
Prone Area Programme (DPAP), Crop Production Manage ment Programme, 
Integrated Scheme of Oilseeds, Pulses, Oilpalm and Maize (ISOPOM), 
Development and Distribution of High Yielding Varie ty (HYV) Seeds, Use 
of Bio-technology, Integrated Nutrient Management ( INM), National Project 
on Organic Farming (NPOF), Integrated Pest Manageme nt (IPM), Farm 
Mechanization, Technology Mission for Integrated De velopment of 
Horticulture, Macro Irrigation, etc. for boosting a gricultural production in the 
country. The Indian Council of Agricultural Researc h (ICAR) and the State 
Agricultural Universities (SAUs) are also contribut ing to the development of 
new technologies for boosting agricultural production.

Subsidies for Chemical Fertilizers  
2763. KUMARI NIRMALA DESHPANDE: Will the Minister o f 
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) how much subsidy is being given for Chemical Fertilizers; 
(b) whether there is any provision for giving subsidy for organic fertilizers and 
for products of organic farming; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefore? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS (SHRI B.K. HANDIQUE): (a) During the fi nancial year 
2006-07, Rs. 25,952.91 crore has been paid as subsi dy for Chemical 
Fertilizers. 
(b) and (c) Organic fertilizers is a subject matter of Ministry of Agriculture and 
Cooperation. At present no subsidy is provided by D epartment of Agriculture 
and Cooperation on organic fertilizers. However fin ancial assistance is being 
provided under the National Project on Organic Farming for setting up of organic 
input production units and also for promotion, trai ning and demonstration on 
organic fertilizers. Financial assistance is being provided for the following 
organic production units:— 
(i) Fruit/vegetable waste compost units - 25% of the total cost subject 
to a maximum of Rs. 40.00 lakh per unit.   
114 

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(ii) Bio-fertilizer production units - 25% of the total cost subject to a 
maximum of Rs. 20.00 lakh per unit. 
(iii) Vermiculture hatcheries - 25% of the total cost subject to a maximum of Rs. 
1.50 lakh per unit. 
The assistance to production unit is being provided as credit linked and back 
ended subsidy through NABARD/NCDC. 
Prices of Essential Drugs  
2764. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that prices of essenti al drugs are not 
affordable even by middle class; 
(b) whether Government are taking any steps to make dru g prices 
affordable by the poor; 
(c) if so, whether target date has been fixed for domestic pharma industry for 
reducing drug prices; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS (SHRI B.K. HANDIQUE): (a) to (d) The Dr ug Policy as 
announced from time to time is directed towards making available quality drugs 
at reasonable prices to the poor. The 74 bulk drugs specified in the First Schedule 
of .the Drugs (Prices-Control) Order, 1995 (DPCO, 9 5) and the formulations 
based thereon are under price control and their prices are fixed/revised by the 
National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) in  accordance with the 
provisions of the DPCO, 95. These drugs have been kept under price control on 
the basis of criteria mentioned in Modifications in Drug Policy, 1966, announced 
in September, 1994. The price fixation/ revision of  the Scheduled Drugs and 
formulations is a continuous process under DPCO, 95. In case of any violation 
of the price fixed by NPPA, action for recovery of overcharging amount is 
taken by NPPA. Hence, prices of medicines under pri ce control have been 
effectively controlled and kept low. 
115 

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
Prices of non-Scheduled formulations are fixed by t he manufacturers 
themselves keeping in view the various factors like  cost of production, 
marketing/selling expenses, R&D expenses, trade com mission, market 
competition, product innovation, product quality etc. Prices of these drugs are 
regularly monitored and corrective measures taken where public interest is found to 
be adversely affected. 
The Government has drafted National Pharmaceutical Policy-2006. After 
the_Policy has been approved, a new Drugs (Prices Control) Order is proposed 
to be issued. This may include several new measures  for better availability of 
cheaper medicines to the common man. In addition se veral other measures for 
making cheaper medicines available to common man are also being contemplated 
e.g. National Health Insurance Policy for the BPL families. Larger allocation for 
National illness Assistance Fund/State illness Assistance Funds. District illness 
Assistance Fund, Revolving Funds for BPL families t o be set up in all the 
Central Government hospitals. Slates also to set up  revolving funds in all the 
Government hospitals for free treatment of BPL, families, Rajasthan model of 
Medicare Relief Societies to be replicated in other  States. Scheme of District 
level Drug Bank in States/UTs, Setting up of Cancer  Medicines Assistance 
Fund etc. Besides, it is also proposed to strengthen NPPA for effective monitoring 
and enforcement of drug prices with the help of State Drug Controllers. 
The Cabinet Note on National Pharmaceuticals Policy -2006 was 
considered by the Cabinet in its meeting held on 11 -1-2007. The Cabinet has 
decided that the matter may, in the first instance, be considered by a Group of 
Ministers (GoM). A Group of Ministers has been constituted. The 1st meeting of 
the GoM was held on 10.4.2007. No specific time fra me can be mentioned 
about the announcement of Policy.

SINGH): (a) No, Sir. PDS in the country is not a failure. 
(b) The PDS is operated under the joint responsibility of the Central and State 
Governments. The Central Government has taken the r esponsibility for 
procurement, storage, transportation and bulk allocation of foodgrains, etc. The 
responsibility for effectively distributing the same to the consumers through the 
network of Fair Price Shops (FPSs) lies with the St ate Governments. The

Effect of organised retail on employment  
2766. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY: Will the Minister of CO NSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that unorganized retailing is a major contributor in the 
rural employment, next to agriculture; 
(b) if so, the data of unorganized retailing in terms o f employment 
generation; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that the growing organized sector in retail would 
affect this unorganized retailing badly; and 
(d) if so, Government's assessment thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI TASLIMUDDIN): 
(a) and (b) As per two latest quinquennial rounds o f National Sample Survey 
Organization on employment and unemployment, employ ment opportunities 
on Current Daily Status basis in trade, hotel and restaurant sector (including retail 
trade) have been estimated at 37.58 million in 1999-2000 (55th round) and at 
47.99 million in 2004-05 (61st round). In rural are as alone, employment 
opportunities in this sector have been estimated at 14.73 million in 1999-2000 and 
20.49 million in 2004-05. Employment in agriculture sector in rural areas was 
estimated'at 185.04 million in 1999-2000 and 192.47  million in 2004-05. In 
terms of percentage share in total employment in ru ral areas, agriculture 
provided employment to 73.68% and 69.37% in 1999-20 00 and 2004-05 
respectively. Share of trade, hotel and restaurant sector in total employment was 
estimated at 5.87% in 1999-2000 and at 7.39% in 2004-05. Data is not available 
separately on employment in retail sector. 
(c) and (d) Department of Industrial Policy and Pro motion have on 20-03-
2007 sanctioned a Study on "The Impact of organized  Retailing on the 
Unorganized Retail Sector" to be carried out by Int ernational Council for 
Research on International Economic Relations (ICRIER). The Study will, inter 
alia, cover effect on small retailers and vendors in the unorganized sector keeping in 
mind the likely growth in the overall market and effect on employment. The Report 
from ICRIER in this regard is expected by middle of July, 2007.

SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUB LIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a decision has been taken  to give economic 
incentive to sugar mills to increase the export of sugar due to its excess 
production in comparison t6 its requirement for consumption in the country in 
2006-07; 
(b) if so, the facts in this regard and the amount of e conomic incentive per 
tonne; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that it was not possible to increase the export 
of sugar from the country without giving economic incentive; and 
(d) if so, the reaction of Government thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, 
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH): 
(a) and (b) The sugar production in the current sug ar season 2006-07 is 
provisionally estiamted at 250 lac tons as against the estimated consumption of 190 
lac tons. Inorder to liquidate the surplus stocks o f sugar and to ensure that 
excess production of sugar does not lead to situation of mounting cane price arrears, the 
Government have decided, inter alia, to provide export assistance to defray the cost 
of internal freight and transport charges, marketing and handling charges at the flat 
rate of Rs. 1350 per ton on export of domestically manufactured sugar from sugar 
factories location in the coastal States and at the flat rate of Rs. 1450 per ton from 
sugar factories located in other than the coastal States. Exports made under Open 
General License (OGL) only (and not under 'advance license') on or after 19th 
April, 2007 and up to 18th April 2008 or till further orders, whichever is earlier,would 
be eligible for this assistance. Further, the amount so received is also to be used for 
payment of cane price including cane price arrears of previous sugar season(s),

factories as realization from export of sugar was less than the

from the molasses route.

 2769.     SHRI MAHMOODA. MADANI: 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUB LIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) how many commodity exchanges are functioning in the country; 
(b) whether Government have taken note of the eligibili ty criterion to 
become the member of these commodity exchanges and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether such criterion facilitate the primary produ cers particularly the 
farmers to become members and trade directly in such exchanges; and 
(d) if not, how such exchanges benefit the primary producers and 
farmers? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI TASLIMUDDIN): (a) 
There are 24 commodity exchanges recognized by the Government under the 
Forward Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1952. 
(b) Articles of Association/Rules of the recognized Exc hanges provide for 
criteria for admission of the members. As per the A rticles/Rules of the 
recognized Exchanges, any individualy/person who is  a citizen of India, and 
who has completed 21 years of age, co-operative societies, corporate bodies etc. 
that complies with the minimum networth criteria, c apital adequacy, minimum 
security deposit, admission fee, registration condi tions as specified in the 
Rules/Articles of the commodity Exchanges recognized by the Government are 
eligible to apply for the membership of these Exchanges. 
(c) and (d) Primary producers including farmers can als o become members 
of the Exchanges subject to their fulfilment of eli gibility criteria. Besides, 
primary producers, farmers, other individuals etc. can trade on the Exchanges 
through members by becoming their clients. They can  benefit from the price 
signals emanating from the commodity futures market and also by hedging.

expected higher global surpluses. The ex-mill prices of sugar in the month of 
March, 2007 were lower by Rs. 200-410 per quintal c ompared to prices at the

farmers. In order to ensure that over production of  sugar does not lead to a 
situation of mounting cane price arrears, Government have decided:— 
(i) to create a buffer stock of 20 lac tons for a period of one year (01 -05-2007 to

charges for the quantity taken as buffer will be re imbursed to sugar 
factories. The coast of this subsidy is estimated to be Rs. 378 crores for 
one year. Further, banks would provide additional credit of Rs. 420 crores 
on creation of 20 lac tons of buffer. Thus, Rs. 798 crores would be available 
with sugar factories to pay can price to sugarcane farmes, for the sugar season 
2006-07 including the cane price arrears of previous sugar seasons. The 
buffer subsidy and the additional credit are to be used exclusively for the 
payment of cane prices.

Statement  
Details of the steps taken by the FCI to preserve the stocks in storage and for 
preventing damaged foodgrains.  
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
131 

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
With a view to preserving the stocks in storage and preventing damage to 
foodgrains, the FCI has been taking the following steps:— 
i. Ensuring that all its own godowns are constructe d and maintained on 
scientific lines for storage of foodgrains. 
ii. Provision for adequate dunnage and plinth for storage of foodgrains in open 
in Cover and Plinth (CAP) storage with covering of specifically fabricated 
low-density black polythene water proof sheets with proper lashing by nylon 
ropes/nets. 
iii. Regular periodic inspections of the stocks/god owns by qualified and 
trained staff. 
iv. Undertaking of prophylactic and curative treatm ents of the stocks 
regularly. 
v. Undertaking the pest control measures regularly. 
vi. Implementation of the procedure of "First in, F irst out" (FIFO) to extent 
possible so as to avoid longer retention of stocks. 
vii. Movement of foodgrains from one place to anoth er by safe means, i.e., 
covered wagons, etc. 
viii. Undertaking pre-monsoon fumigation. 
ix. Improvement in dunnage material. 
x. Policy guidelines has been issued to State Governments for proper storage 
and timely offtake of wheat stocks from getting damaged. 
xi. Stocks of foodgrains are treated with malathion  and deltamethrin as a 
preventive measures to arrest infestation regularly  on fortnightly & 
quarterly basis respectively. 
xii. Whenever infestation is noticed stocks are fum igated with Aluminum 
Phosphide, as a curative measures.. 
xiii. In order to guage the condition/health of sto cks, they are classified and 
categorized, every fortnight by the Technical Assis tance, which are 
supervised on monthly basis by his supervisory Manager (QC) in the depot. 
xiv. To oversee, as to whether stocks are properly preserved and stored, Senior 
QC officers such as Asstt. Genl. Manager (QC) and Dy. Genl. 
132 

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
Manager (QC) also check the stocks once in a quarter and 10 depots in a 
month respectively under their respective jurisdiction. 
xv. Apart from above, Area Manager of the FCI district, General Manager of the 
Region and Executive Director of the Zone also insp ect 2 depots in a 
district, 2 depots in a region and at least one depot in the zone respectively 
once in a month. 
xvi. All the Inspection Reports of the above mentio ned officers are critically 
examined at Regional and Zonal level and closely monitored at the FCI, 
Hqrs. and action on any discrepancy/short fall observed in these reports are 
promptly taken. 
Every case of occurrence of damaged foodgrains is invariably investigated and 
wherever stocks found damaged due to negligence on the part of officials, 
stern disciplinary action is taken. 
It has, recently been decided that in case of accru al of more than one 
thousand metric tones of damaged foodgrain, in any region, the FCI

Melting of Himalayan Glaciers 
2790. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that the Himalayan Glaciers are having 
cracks and are rapidly melting; 
(b) if so, whether there is any possibility of floods and evalaunching of snow 
on the mountains which would affect the large population; 
(c) how far such melting and evalaunching of snow shall have adverse affects 
on the rivers particularly in Northern India; and 
(d) the steps being proposed to be taken for the protection of the public and the 
agricultural fields? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) The studies c arried out by 
Geological Survey of India have revealed that the Himalayan Glaciers, like any 
other glaciers in the world, have cracks. Such crac ks are result of the various 
forces acting on the glaciers and not necessarily due to the melting of the glaciers 
alone. However, it is also true that Himalayan Glac iers are passing through a 
phase of recession, which is a worldwide phenomenon. Such recession could also 
be attributed to the phenomenon of global warming. 
(b) During winters, avalanching in the mountains is  a common 
phenomenon which is not related to the development of cracks and melting 
of the glaciers. As far as glaciers are concerned, majority of glaciers in 
Himalaya are located in very remote areas where no population resides 
and therefore are not a threat. The marginal increa se in the river discharge 
due to melting of glaciers may not lead to heavy fl oods in the rivers affecting 
population. 
(c) Melting of glaciers may cause marginal rise in the water discharge of 
rivers in Northern India. However, as this process is very slow, it may not have any 
major adverse affect on the rivers. 
(d) The measures taken to reduce the recession of glaci ers include 
conservation activities such as afforestation, removal of garbage, restrictions on 
human interference on glaciers and promotion of sustainable eco-tourism.

Medicine for reducing the lipid level in the blood  
†2806. SHRI MAHENDRA SAHNI: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND

research have recently invented a new medicine to lessen the content of lipid and 
sugar in the blood;

(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) to (c) According to the 
Indian Council of Medical Research, a project funded by the Councifin the Deptt. 
of Biochemistry, University College of Medical Science, Delhi has succeeded in 
isolating an active hypoglycemic compound from the pulp of black plum fruit 
Jamun. The four compounds isolated from the pulp when tested in animals have 
been found to reduce blood sugar. As this new product also reduces the blood 
level of cholesterol, it may prove to be effective in Diabetes mellitus, 
especially those having associated heart diseases. According to the Council, US

only after proving the safety and efficacy of the compounds in clinical trials and 
technology transfer.

(b) To controtTB, the Revised National TB Control Programme (RNTCP) based 
on WHO recommended Directly observed Treatment Shor t-course strategy, 
widely known as DOTS was implemented in the country  in a phased manner 
from 1997 and the entire country had ben covered by March 2006. The objective of 
the programme was to achieve and maintain a cure ra te of 85% amongst new 
sputum positive cases and to detect and maintain a case detection rate of at least 70 
amongst such cases. 
Under Revised National TB Control Programme, diagnosis is made by quality 
assured sputum curing infectious cases on priority.  Facilities for diagnosis by 
sputum microscopy have been decentralized and stren gthened. Drugs are 
provided under observation of a DOTS provider and patients are monitored so 
that they complete their treatment. Drugs are provided free of cost inpatient-wise 
boxes. Till date, the Revised National TB Control Programme has placed more than 
69.30 lakh patients on DOTS treatment averting more than 12.40 lakh deaths. 
Every month more than 1.2 lakh patients are placed on DOTS. In 2006 alone, 
India palced more than 13.97 lakhs cases on DOTS, more than any country in a 
single year in the world. Overall performance of Re vised National TB Control 
Programme has been excellent with cure/treatment completion rate consistently 
above 85% and death rate reduced to less than 5%. To increase accessibility of 
the masses to the facilities provided under the Pro gramme, special emphasis is 
laid on the IEC activities, involvement of NGOs, pr ivate sector and medical 
colleges in the revised strategy.

2826. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that most of the countries including US 
have imposed stringent regulations on DDT maximum Residue Level in food 
products; 
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that Codex India has been openly favouring DDT 
levels of five mg per kg of poultry or meat; 
(c) MRL prescribed by WHO and FAO in this regard;

details thereof, and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
181 

RAJYA SABHA    . [27 April, 2007] 
(e) whether Government propose any steps to safeguard the health of people 
who buy high level DDT MRL food products? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) to (e) In the country, there is a ban on the use of DDT in agriculture. DDT 
is, however, allowed to be used for vector control (Malaria Programme) in the 
country. 
The Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) for DDT in various food commodities has 
been prescribed under Prevention of foods commoditi es has been prescribed 
under Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1995 for the reason that even though, it 
is not permitted to be used in agriculture, DDT bei ng one of the pesticides, 
which persists in the environment, it is generally detected in food 
commodities, feed and fodder. 
The Maximum Tolerance Limits (MTL) for DDT on Meat, Poultry and fish 
(on whole product basis) has been prescribed as 7.0  ppm. in consultation with 
the Central Committee for Food Standards (CCFS), th e statutory committee 
under the PFA Act, 1954 to advise the Central Gover nment on 
implementation of the Act. 
The current Codex level (as in 2006) for DDT in meat (from mammals other 
than marine mammals) is 5.0 mg/kg (on fat basis) and in poultry meat, it is 0.3 
mg/kg. During 35th Session of Codex Committee on Pe sticide Residues 
(CCPR) held in 2003, there was a proposal to revise the current level for DDT 
in meat from 5 mg/kg to 1 mg/kg. India had proposed  in their comments that 
Extraneous Maximum Residies Limit (EMRL) for DDT on  meat should be 
retained at 5 mg/kg (on fat basis), which ensures c onsumer protection. Fixation 
of a lower level, on the other hand might result in  difficulty of exports from 
India.

Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be p leased to 
state: 
(a) whether the Supreme Court in January, 2007 pulled u p the Centre and 
States for tardy implementation of the 100 per cent Centrally sponsored National 
Maternity Benefit Scheme to Below Poverty Line families; 
(b) if so, whether State Governments implemented the sc heme to a bare 
minimum level and left with huge unutilized funds despite receiving dwindling 
outlays every successive year from the Centre; 
(c) whether Government have failed to monitor the scheme effectively; 
(d) the total number of families benefited up till now; and 
(e) the steps the Central and State Governments have taken to implement the 
scheme and utilized the funds? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) The Hon'ble Supreme 
Court while hearing the writ petition (Civil) regarding PUCL Versus Union of India 
and other, expressed concern over the low utilisation of funds by the States under 
National Maternity Benefits Scheme(NMBS). 
(b) and (c) Due to poor implementation of the schem e by the States/ Union 
Territories(UT), many States could not utilise the allocated fund, As a result, the 
States could not furnish utilisation certificates i n time. Although, Central 
Government had sufficient money, the same could not be released to these States. 
The matter regarding low utilisation of fund has be en discussed with States in 
several meetings and follow-up communications. With regards to the pending 
utilisation certificates, it is being vigorously fo llowed up. As the core 
responsibility of implementation of National Matern ity Benefit Scheme was 
with the States/UTs, they were advised to closely monitor the implementation. 
(d) During its operation from 1995-96 to 2004-05, a pproximately 1.20 
crores.pregnant women have benefited under the scheme.. 
186 

[27 April, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(e) Due to low utilisation of fund and also due to the fact that the scheme was not 
addressing the maternal health issues holistically,  the scheme has been 
modified into a new scheme namely Janani Suraksha Y ojana providing cash 
benefits alongwith maternity services. The new sche me has been introduced 
with effect from April, 2005. In the States having low level of health indicators, 
impeding parameters like BPL certification, party and age have been removed. 
Besides, the quantum of cash benefits has been incr eased to Rs. 1400/- per 
delivery in rural areas. For quick disbursement of cash benefit, money is 
disbursed through ANM &ASHA. In addition, Gram Panchayat is also invovled 
in the disbursement of cash. The Central Government has funded the State to 
set up progamme management units at the State, district and even at block level, 
under the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) 
Since the introduction of Janani Surakha Yojana (JSY), majority of the States 
have been reporting higher expenditure. Against app roximately 5.7 lakhs 
beneficiaries reported in the financial year 2005-06, around 21 lakh pregnant 
women have benefited from this scheme till February, 2007, in the year 2006-07. 
An amount of Rs, 261.00 crores has been released to  States/UTs in the year 
2006-07 for Janani Suraksha Yojana. 
Maternal Mortality Ratio in the country  
2830. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that according to UNICEF, Indi a has high maternal 
mortality ratio at 301 per 1,00,000 live births; 
(b) whether it is a fact that the UNICEF has launched a  new scheme to 
conduct probe into maternal deaths; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) UNICEF has  not 
conducted any survey to ascertain Maternal Mortalit y Ratio in India and uses 
official published data for reference. Based on the official estimates of Regisfrar 
General of India (RGI) (SRS 2001-03), the Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) for 
India is 301 per 1,00,000 live births. 
187 

RAJYA SABHA [27 April, 2007] 
(b) UNICEF in collaboration with John Hopkins University, USA and the State 
Government has developed a comprehensive toolkit fo r retrospective verbal 
autopsy of maternal deaths and method for providing feedback for community 
action. 
(c) UNICEF is working with various State Governments to  help them 
streamline their existing maternal death audit prot ocols and practices. It is 
currently supporting the implementation of maternal death enquiry in five high 
maternal mortality States namely Jharkhand, Orissa,  Madhya Pradesh, 
Rajasthan and West Bengal since 2004-2005. UNICEF i s supporting the 
Development and Implementation of Maternal and Perinatal (Child Death within 7 
days of birth) Death Enquiries (MAPEDE) as a tool to strengthen commounitv 
participation in evidence based district level planning in above States. The tool, 
which is basically a structured verbal autopsy questionnaire, has been given to the 
respective States by UNICEF.

2833. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the survey done by WHO in which it 
was assessed that by 2020 the country will have alm ost one-fourth of its 
population affected with different degrees of mental ill health; and

rehabilitation, proper treatment and attention for such patients? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY

Health Report, 2001, it is estimated that Disabilit y Adjusted Life Year

mental healthcare to such patients through District Mental Health Programme at 
the Primary Health Care and District Level. As a me dium and long term 
strategy, infrastructure development and capacity building is being undertaken in 
the field of mental health by modernization of Ment al Hospitals and

†2853. SHRIMATI SUSHMA SWARAJ: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS

in place of these dilapidated bridges? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI R. 
VELU): (a) There are approximately 1,27,000 railway  bridges on Indian 
Railway system. Out of this, about 51,000 no. of Br idges are more than 100 
years old. 
(b) to (d) The life of a railway bridge is not base d on its age but on 
physical condition as ascertained by inspections. R ailways have a well laid 
down system of multi-tier inspection of Bridges. Ra ilway undertakes repair, 
rehabilitation/rebuilding of bridges on the basis o f their physical condition as 
ascertained during inspection and not on the basis of age. Few bridges which 
may show signs of deterioration of physical conditi on indicating need for 
rehabilitation are classified as Distressed Bridges . These, however, are 
neither unsafe nor dilapidated bridges. Based on su ch identification of 
bridges, allotment of funds is made annually to car ry out their repair, 
rehabilitation/rebuilding duly prioritizing the work as per requirement. 
In 2001-02, to clear the backlog of-replacement of such identified bridges 
on Indian Railways, 2370 bridges were sanctioned fo r repair/ 
rehabilitation/rebuilding at a cost of Rs. 1530 Cro re (Net) under Special 
Railway Safety Fund (SRSF). Apart from SRSF, additi onal funds are also 
made available annually in Railway Budget to undert ake repair/ rehabilitation

impact of big industries on SSI 
 2876. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the Minister of SMALL SCALE 
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Small Scale Industries ar e being crippled 
because of the competition from big industries and the multinationals; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that the number of items reserved for SSI has 
been gradually reduced; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps Government would take to help the SSI to withstand the 
competition from big industrial and the multinationals? 
THE MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTIRES (SHRI MAHAVt R 
PRASAD): (a) No specific reports are available giving the extent to which Indian 
small scale industries as a whole may have been aff ected due to competition 
from big industries and multi-national corporations (MNCs). However, from the 
fact that the annual rate of growth of production of the SSI sector has so far been 
consistently higher than that of the country's industrial sector as a whole, it can 
be inferred that the SSI sector has generally been able to face up to the 
competition in the market, including that from the big industries and MNCs. 
(b) and (c) The Government has been following a policy of progressive de-
reservation of such items. Review of the list of su ch reserved items is a 
continuous process, during which creation of opport unities for higher 
investment, facilitating technological upgradation,  improving quality, 
promoting exports and achieving economies of scale in manufacturing the said 
items are kept in mind. Allowing domestic competiti on to check large-scale 
imports of such reserved items is also an issue considered by the Government. 
(d) To enhance the competitiveness of the SSI units  vis-a-vis the big 
industries and MNCs, the Government have put in place several measures, which 
include assistance for technological upgradation, accessing markets, improved 
infrastructure, better availability of credit, faci lities for training and capacity 
building of entrepreneurs, etc.
